clauses.statement: An enumeration scenario is accepted only in the form 'enumeration: grepped <identifier> across <paths>; <N> sites found, <M> updated, <K> unchanged because <reason>'; count-free narration, a missing searchable path, and a non-identifier subject are rejected with a typed reason, and scenarios that do not declare themselves as enumeration claims pass through unchanged.

test_refs.case: ENUM-S-1 parses a well formed enumeration scenario into structured parts
ENUM-S-1 rejects count-free narration that announces itself as enumeration

clauses.statement: Enumeration counts must partition the discovered sites: N equals M plus K, N is at least 1, and any K greater than zero requires an explicit because clause; a claim violating any of these is rejected at verify record time rather than stored.

test_refs.case: ENUM-S-2 rejects counts that do not partition the discovered sites
ENUM-S-2 rejects a zero-site sweep as a discovery failure, not coverage
ENUM-S-2 requires a reason whenever sites are deliberately left unchanged

clauses.statement: scenario_clause_e2e: the claimed site count is recounted against the tree over the same declared range with whole-token matching, and a claim whose number does not match the observed number, or whose declared path does not exist or escapes the repository, fails closed; writing the token alone never satisfies the gate.

test_refs.case: ENUM-S-3 fails closed when the claimed count does not match the recount
ENUM-S-3 fails closed when a declared path does not exist
ENUM-S-3 passes only when the claimed count survives the recount

clauses.statement: Enumeration is required only for identifiers introduced by the change and present in two or more product source files at head; pre-existing vocabulary and single-file constants are skipped with a recorded reason, a change with no such identifier resolves as not_applicable, and an unreadable base tree resolves as inconclusive rather than a pass.

test_refs.case: ENUM-S-4 requires enumeration only for new identifiers spanning 2+ source files
ENUM-S-4 treats a docs-only change (no product source diff) as not_applicable
ENUM-S-4 reports inconclusive, not pass, when the base tree cannot be read

clauses.statement: gate:enumeration_coverage is a required node on the gate DAG between failure_mode_coverage and decision_record, blocks PR creation and managed execution in every status other than passed and not_applicable, and publishes the reproduction grep and the verify record template for each identifier still missing a claim.

test_refs.case: ENUM-S-5 reports needs_evidence when a required identifier has no claim
ENUM-S-5 a claim for a different identifier does not close the required one

clauses.statement: The enumeration coverage workflow moves through explicit states and transitions: a change introducing no cross-file identifier resolves not_applicable; an introduced identifier with no claim transitions to needs_evidence; a recorded claim failing grammar, count partition or recount transitions to failed; an unresolvable base ref transitions to inconclusive; and the process reaches passed only when every introduced identifier carries a claim whose count the gate recounted. Rollback of the whole flow is a single revert leaving recorded evidence intact.

test_refs.case: ENUM-S-4 resolves not_applicable for a change with no new cross-file identifier
ENUM-S-5 reports needs_evidence when a required identifier has no claim
ENUM-S-4 reports inconclusive, not pass, when the base tree cannot be read

diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[verify record --scenario] -->|untrusted claim text| B{grammar check}
  B -->|malformed| R1[reject: enumeration_scenario_malformed]
  B -->|well formed| C{count partition N = M + K}
  C -->|unbalanced| R2[reject: enumeration_counts_unbalanced]
  C -->|balanced| D[(evidence artifact)]
  D --> E{gate recount over declared paths}
  E -->|path escapes repo or absent| R3[fail: enumeration_path_missing]
  E -->|claimed count != observed| R4[fail: enumeration_count_mismatch]
  E -->|stale binding| R5[claim ignored]
  E -->|match| P[gate:enumeration_coverage passed]
diagrams.rationale: Spec clause C-003 and Story AC ENUM-S-3. The scenario string is operator-supplied text that asserts a fact about the tree, so the trust boundary is between the claim and the tree. Threats are a fabricated count, a path outside the repository used to inflate or redirect the scan, and a claim recorded against a tree that has since changed; each is closed by recount, containment check and binding respectively.
